concerns.concern: The paper gives mutually incompatible energies for the bulk gap edges. On its own assignment, with the VBM at about −10 meV, the claimed edge peak at E_F sits essentially at the valence-band edge rather than inside the gap.
concerns.quote: The center spectrum exhibits a V-shaped dip between ±50 mV, whereas the edge spectrum displays a pronounced peak at EF within the same energy range

concerns.concern: Edge spectra cover only about ±0.1 V and the map is taken at a single energy (+7 mV). A topological edge mode should show enhanced weight across the whole ~300 meV gap, and that is not demonstrated.
concerns.quote: Figures 5(d) and (e) present a map acquired at the energy of the edge states

concerns.concern: Claiming 'realization of the QSH phase' overstates the evidence. The substrate is metallic, there is no spin or transport evidence, and edge states have not been shown across the gap. 'Independent of step geometry' is also unsupported.
concerns.quote: we report the first experimental realization of the QSH phase in ML-Si2Te2

concerns.concern: A sharp dI/dV peak is not the generic signature of a linearly dispersing 1D helical mode, whose DOS should be flat. The computed edge LDOS lineshape is never compared with the measured peak in the main text.
concerns.quote: 1D topological edge states in ML-Si2Te2 are expected to manifest as a dI/dV peak near the edge, consistent with the sharp feature

concerns.concern: The edge contrast in the dI/dV map may be an artifact of the constant-current setpoint (Vstab inside the gap, abrupt step height). Bright interior patches and the missing ring segment, blamed on the tip, are not explained.
concerns.quote: taken at +7 mV, corresponding to the area shown in (d)

concerns.concern: A 2–3 nm spatial extent does not rule out trivial edge or band-bending states. Calling 2–3 nm a 'good agreement' with the DFT value of 1.35 nm from a free-standing ribbon is loose.
concerns.quote: supports its topological origin and rules out trivial mechanisms such as lattice defects or dangling bonds

concerns.concern: The Z2 invariant is computed via Wannier charge centers for a heterostructure that is metallic. The band manifold used, and whether it has a direct gap at every k, is not stated.
concerns.quote: the WCCs curves for both the heterostructure and the free-standing ML-Si2Te2 cross an arbitrary horizontal reference line an odd number of times

concerns.concern: The Z2/WCC method is cited to the wrong reference. Ref. [39] should be replaced by the standard Soluyanov & Vanderbilt and/or Yu et al. papers.
concerns.quote: Ref. [39] (Giustino & Pasquarello, mixed Wannier–Bloch functions) is not the standard reference for WCC-based Z2

concerns.concern: Matching the measured ~300 meV gap to 319 meV by subtracting the ML-HfTe2 VBM offset looks post hoc, since the experiment uses bulk semimetallic HfTe2. The combined system has no global gap, so it is not an isolated QSH insulator.
concerns.quote: Given that the valance band maximum (VBM) of ML-HfTe2 lies 110 meV above that of ML-Si2Te2

concerns.concern: The commensurate 1×1 DFT cell forces both layers to a common lattice constant, so the 'strain-free' result is partly built in. The HfTe2 compression this implies, and the residual strain on each layer, should be reported.
concerns.quote: After full structural relaxation, the in-plane lattice constants of ML-Si2Te2 remain at aDFT = bDFT = 389 pm, identical to those of free-standing case

concerns.concern: A measured 390 pm Si2Te2 lattice on ~396 pm HfTe2 would be incommensurate, which conflicts with the claimed hollow-site registry. The HfTe2 lattice measured in the same image is not reported, although it would serve as a calibration.
concerns.quote: a 390 pm Si2Te2 lattice on a ~396 pm HfTe2 surface would be incommensurate

concerns.concern: The sign convention for the lattice mismatch Δ appears to invert the asymmetric strain window. This could change which substrates pass the screen, with HfTe2 sitting at the edge of the window.

The substrate-enhanced gap of 429 meV (HSE06, heterostructure) is compared with 220 meV that may be PBE-level. The increase may be a functional effect rather than a substrate effect, and the free-standing HSE06 gap is not given in the main text.
concerns.quote: enhancing its nontrivial band gap to 429 meV

concerns.concern: The number of screening candidates in the text (76) contradicts Fig. 1(a) (65 TMDs).
The measured step height (710 pm) is about 10% below the calculated spacing (790 pm), and bias-dependent apparent height is not discussed. Ref. [40] is an odd source for this comparison.
concerns.quote: is in reasonable agreement with the calculated interlayer spacing [29, 40]

concerns.concern: The ~0.25 eV DFT/STS energy offset is blamed on substrate doping, even though the DFT model includes the substrate and predicts the opposite E_F position. Its direction and origin need justification.
concerns.quote: substrate-induced doping effect that are not fully captured in DFT model

concerns.concern: The growth recipe is underspecified, with no absolute fluxes, Si:Te ratio, or annealing time. The drop in coverage above 320 °C sits oddly with high quality at 385 °C.
concerns.quote: we continuously supplied both Si and Te fluxes exceeding 20 times the nominal co-evaporation rate during annealing

concerns.concern: The supplementary-material description in Ref. [35] mentions 'three stripe orientations' that do not appear in this work. It seems copied from another manuscript and misdescribes the Supplement.
concerns.quote: large area scans showing the coexistence of three stripe orientations.
